candidates.title: All AI-generated code should be Open Source
candidates.author: jcubic
candidates.content_excerpt: All AI-generated code should be Open Source Skip to main content This may be a hot take, but I strongly believe that all code generated by AI should be Open Source. And here's why. First of all, AI models were trained on a massive corpus of Open Source code written since RMS announced the GNU Project and the Free Software Movement. That code was simply scraped from the internet and used without permission or proper attribution. The models were also trained on Stack Overflow and Stack Exchange sister projects, which are released under Creative Commons licenses that legally require attribution. Turning this collective knowledge into proprietary, closed-source code feels like license laundering. candidates.title: Ask HN: What are the most useful, concrete AI skills to independently learn?
candidates.author: shnock
candidates.content_excerpt: Specifically, what are the most useful, concrete skills to learn as an individual to take economic advantage of the advances in LLMs, agents and associated new technological capabilities? What is accessible to learn just from the internet and experimentation, without a degree program, assuming a preexisting moderately technical background? The clearer and more specific (eg. “Learn how-to x with y”) the better. Thank you! Get a 7B model running locally before you touch any API. A quantized 7B is around 4.7GB and runs on a 16GB laptop with no GPU, via llama.cpp. The cost saving is not the point.
